cases.detail: Verilator 5.052 uses the host thread/context RNG for $urandom, so separately seeded design processes interfere when clocked independently. IEEE 1800-2023 18.14.1-2 requires a separate stream per SystemVerilog process, independent of thread execution order. The shared case seeds two module-instance processes identically and compares their streams after alternating activations.

cases.detail: Verilator 5.052 treats a zero $urandom seed as an entropy request, so reseeding with zero does not reproduce the sequence. IEEE 1800-2023 18.13.1 permits any integral seed and requires the same sequence for the same seed. A standalone run reports zero_seed_repeat=0 in Verilator and 1 in Icarus; nonzero seeding repeats in both.

cases.detail: Verilator 5.052 moves an unseeded $urandom draw before the preceding seeded call when optimizing the clocked body, breaking the reseeded reference sequence. Its generated C++ assigns second from VL_RANDOM_I before the preceding VL_URANDOM_SEEDED_II call. IEEE 1800-2023 18.13.1 requires the seed to determine the following stream; 18.14.2 localizes its state to the calling process. The original sequential assertions, short circuits and indexed draw are preserved.
